results.content: Nationally, voters say they prefer Democratic candidates over Republicans by an eight-point margin – slightly more modest than their 12-point advantage in CNN’s September polling ahead of the 2018 midterms in Trump’s first presidency. But Trump is even more unpopular than he was in 2018, and the economic backdrop has worsened considerably. Now, just 27% of Americans approve of Trump on the economy, down 22 points from 2018. The issue has risen in prominence: Two-thirds of registered voters call the economy “extremely important” to their vote, higher than in the autumn before either of the past two midterms. A new Economist/YouGov poll released Sept. 22 found Trump's approval rating fell five points in a single week, from 40% to 35%, wiping out five straight weeks of gains in the same poll. The drop leaves him just two points above the lowest rating he's ever recorded in the survey and comes as Republicans enter the final stretch before November's midterm elections. [...] The Economist/YouGov survey was conducted Sept. 18-21 among 1,402 registered voters and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.4 percentage points.
